content: 1. Acalabrutinib metabolism is influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor is necessary (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 2. Acetazolamide may increase cobicistat levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 3. Cobicistat increases adagrasib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of adagrasib, a CYP3A4 substrate, with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until adagrasib concentrations reach steady-state (~8 days). If steady-state is not achieved, coadministration may increase adagrasib concentrations and toxicity risk. 4. Cobicistat increases ado-trastuzumab emtansine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Cobicistat increases alfentanil levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 6. Cobicistat increases alfuzosin levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the potential for serious or life-threatening reactions, such as hypotension. 7. Cobicistat increases alpelisib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with a BCRP inhibitor may increase alpelisib concentrations and toxicity risk. If unavoidable, closely monitor for adverse reactions. 8. Cobicistat increases alprazolam levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 9. Cobicistat increases amiodarone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. 10. Cobicistat increases amitriptyline levels or effects by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose and monitoring for response. 11. Cobicistat increases amlodipine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Cobicistat increases amoxapine levels or effects by altering CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose and monitoring for response. 13. Anastrozole may increase cobicistat levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 14. Cobicistat increases apalutamide levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce exposure to CYP3A4 substrates, potentially leading to therapeutic failure. 15. Cobicistat increases apixaban levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 16. Cobicistat increases aprepitant levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Cobicistat increases aripiprazole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce aripiprazole dose by 25%, or by approximately 50% if coadministered with both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibitors. 18. Cobicistat increases armodafinil levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Armodafinil, a CYP3A4 inducer, may decrease cobicistat levels. 19. Cobicistat may decrease the efficacy of artemether/lumefantrine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for reduced antimalarial efficacy or QT prolongation. 20. Cobicistat increases astemizole levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 21. Atazanavir increases cobicistat levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and vice versa. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Cobicistat increases atogepant levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust atogepant dosage to 10 mg daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Cobicistat increases atorvastatin levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 24. Cobicistat increases avanafil levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as safe and effective dosing for avanafil has not been established. 25. Cobicistat increases avapritinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Cobicistat increases avatrombopag levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. When treating ITP, reduce the avatrombopag starting dose if coadministered with moderate or strong dual CYP2C9/3A4 inhibitors. 27. Cobicistat increases axitinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Cobicistat and azithromycin may increase each other's levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Cobicistat increases bedaquiline levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Belzutifan decreases cobicistat levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 31. Cobicistat increases benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 32. Cobicistat increases berotralstat levels by affecting BCRP metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects when coadministered with a BCRP inhibitor. 33. Cobicistat increases betrixaban levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 34. Cobicistat increases bortezomib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Bosentan decreases cobicistat levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of bosentan is required. 36. Cobicistat increases bosentan levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Cobicistat increases bosutinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Cobicistat increases brentuximab vedotin levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Cobicistat increases brexpiprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Cobicistat increases brigatinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce brigatinib dose by 50%. 41. Cobicistat increases bromocriptine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Cobicistat increases budesonide levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Cobicistat increases buprenorphine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 44. Cobicistat increases buspirone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. A reduced dose of buspirone may be required. 45. Cobicistat increases cabozantinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If required, reduce cabozantinib dose and resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuation of the inhibitor. 46. Cobicistat affects calcifediol metabolism by altering CYP3A4. CYP450 inhibitors may inhibit enzymes involved in vitamin D metabolism, potentially altering serum calcifediol levels.
